PREFACE
This Code constitutes a recodification of the general and permanent ordinances of Morgan County, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the 2000 Code, as supplemented through ordinances adopted as of September 12, 2006, and ordinances subsequently adopted by the board of commissioners. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of the 2000 Code, as supplemented, and any subsequent ordinance included herein.
The chapters of the Code have been conveniently arranged in alphabetical order, and the various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage. Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may be included by using one of the reserved chapter numbers. Care should be taken that the alphabetical arrangement of chapters is maintained when including new chapters.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. Indexes
The indexes have been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the indexes themselves which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up-to-date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up-to-date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.

ADOPTING ORDINANCE ORDINANCE OF MAY 1, 2007
AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING AND ENACTING A NEW CODE FOR THE CITY OF MORGAN COUNTY, GEORGIA; PROVIDING FOR THE REPEAL OF CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT INCLUDED THEREIN; PROVIDING A PENALTY FOR THE VIOLATION THEREOF; PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER OF AMENDING SUCH CODE; AND PROVIDING WHEN SUCH CODE AND THIS ORDINANCE SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE.
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CLERK OF THE BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS OF THE COUNTY ATTORNEY'S OFFICE OF THE CITY OF MORGAN COUNTY, GEORGIA:
Section 1. The Code entitled "The Code of Morgan County, Georgia," published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of chapters 1 through 74, each inclusive, is adopted.
Section 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature enacted on or before September 12, 2006, and not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
Section 3. The repeal provided for in section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
Section 4. Unless another penalty is expressly provided, every person convicted of a violation of any provision of the Code or any ordinance, rule or regulation adopted or issued in pursuance thereof shall be punished by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 and costs, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or to both such fine and imprisonment, any or all of such penalties to be imposed at the discretion of the Judge of the Magistrate Court. Each act of violation and each day upon which any such violation shall continue or occur shall constitute a separate offense. The penalty provided by this section, unless another penalty is expressly provided, shall apply to the amendment of any code section, whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the county may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
Section 5. Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in such form as to indicate the intention of the board of commissioners to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
Section 6. Ordinances adopted after September 12, 2006, that amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend or refer to like provisions of the Code.
Section 7. This resolution and the new Code of Morgan County shall become effective upon approval of the second reading of the new Code of Morgan County by the board of commissioners.
Passed and adopted by the board of commissioners this 1st day of May, 2007.

(a) There is created a body corporate and politic, to be known as the "Morgan County Water Authority," which shall be deemed to be a political subdivision of the State of Georgia and a public corporation and by that name, style, and title said body may contract and be contracted with, sue and be sued, implead and be impleaded, and complain and defend in all courts of law and equity.

To be eligible for appointment as a member of the authority, a person shall be at least 21 years of age and a resident of Morgan County for at least one year prior to the date of his appointment and shall not have been convicted of a felony. From and after July 1, 1989, the five members of the authority shall consist of and be selected as provided in this section. Each of the county and municipal governing authorities shall be entitled to appoint one member of the authority. The member appointed by the governing authority of Morgan County shall be appointed for a term of five years and until a successor is appointed and qualified. The member appointed by the governing authority of the City of Madison shall be appointed for a term of four years and until a successor is appointed and qualified. The member appointed by the governing authority of the City of Rutledge shall be appointed for a term of three years and until a successor is appointed and qualified. The member appointed by the governing authority of the City of Bostwick shall be appointed for a term of two years and until a successor is appointed and qualified. The member appointed by the governing authority of the City of Buckhead shall be appointed for a term of two years and until a successor is appointed and qualified. No member appointed by the governing authority of Morgan County shall be a resident of the City of Madison, City of Rutledge, City of Bostwick, or City of Buckhead. Members appointed by the governing authority of a municipality need not be a resident of such municipality. Successors to the members appointed as provided in this subsection shall be appointed by the respective governing authority making the original appointment for terms of five years and until their successors are appointed and qualified. Any member of the authority may be appointed to succeed himself. The authority shall select one of its members as chairman, one as vice-chairman, and one as secretary-treasurer, each of whom shall serve in such respective position for the succeeding year and until his or her successor is selected. Three members shall constitute a quorum.

A vacancy shall exist in the office of any member of the authority who is convicted of a felony or who enters a plea of nolo contendere thereto; who is convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude or who enters a plea of nolo contendere thereto; who moves his residence from the county; who is convicted of any act of misfeasance, malfeasance, or nonfeasance of his duties as a member of the authority; or who fails to attend any five consecutive regular or special meetings of the authority without an excuse approved by a resolution of the authority. No vacancy on the authority shall impair the right of the quorum to exercise all the rights and perform all the duties of the authority. Words and phrases used in this Code shall have the following meanings, unless otherwise specified. In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances, the following rules shall be observed unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the board of commissioners:
General rule. All words and phrases shall be construed and understood according to the common and approved usage of the language; but technical words and phrases and such others as may have acquired a peculiar and appropriate meaning in the law shall be construed and understood according to such peculiar and appropriate meaning.
Advice and consent. The term "advice and consent" means an affirmative vote of the majority of the board of commissioners actually present at the time of the vote.
Board of commissioners, board. The term "board of commissioners" or "board" means the board of commissioners of the County of Morgan, Georgia.
Code. The term "Code" or "this Code" means The Code of Morgan County, Georgia, as designated in section 1-1.
Computation of time. The time within which an act is to be done as provided in any Code provision or ordinance or in any order issued pursuant to any ordinance, when expressed in days, shall be computed by excluding the first day and including the last, except that if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or a legal holiday it shall be excluded; and when any such time is expressed in hours the whole of Sunday, from midnight to midnight, shall be excluded. When the period of time prescribed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
Conjunctions. In a provision involving two or more items, conditions, provisions or events, which items, conditions, provisions or events are connected by the conjunction "and," "or" or "either … or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows:
(1) "And" indicates that all the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply.
(2) "Or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly or in any combination.
(3) "Either … or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly but not in combination.
County. The term "the county" or "this county" means the unincorporated areas of Morgan County, Georgia.
Delegation of authority. Whenever a provision requires the head of a department or other officer of the county to do some act or perform some duty, it shall be construed to authorize subordinates to do the required act or perform the required duty unless the terms of the provision designate otherwise.
Gender. Every word in any Code provision or ordinance importing the masculine or feminine gender shall extend to and be applied to females as well as males or vice-versa as the case may be.
Governing authority or governing body. The term "governing authority" or "governing body" means the board of commissioners of the County of Morgan, Georgia.
Joint authority. All words purporting to give a joint authority to three or more county officers or other persons shall be construed as giving such authority to a majority of such officers or other persons unless it shall be otherwise expressly declared in the law giving the authority.
Judge orrecorder. The term "judge" or "recorder" means the judge of the superior court of the county, the judge of the magistrate court of the county or the judge of any state court of the county, as the case may be.
May. The term "may" is to be construed as being permissive and not mandatory.
May not. The term "may not" states a prohibition.
Number. Every word importing the plural number only shall extend and be applied to one person or thing as well as to several persons or things.
Oath. The term "oath" means an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases the words "affirm" and "affirmed" shall be equivalent to the words "swear" or "sworn."
O.C.G.A. The abbreviation "O.C.G.A." means the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, as amended.
Ordinance. The term "ordinance" means a legislative act of the governing body of a general and permanent nature.
Overlapping provisions. Where any provision of this Code imposes greater restrictions upon the subject matter than any general provisions imposed by this Code, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be applicable.
Owner. The term "owner" means any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, joint tenant by the entirety, of the whole or a part of a building or land.
Person. The term "person" means a corporation, firm, agency, partnership, association, organization, government, and any other group acting as a unit, as well as an individual.
Personal property. The term "personal property" means every type of property except real property.
Preceding and following. The terms "preceding" and "following" mean immediately before and immediately after, respectively.
Property. The term "property" means anything of value, including but not limited to real estate, tangible and intangible personal property, contract rights, services, choices in action, and other interests in or claims to wealth, admission or transportation tickets, captured or domestic animals, food and drink, and electric or other power.
Provision. The term "provision" means any portion or part of this Code.
Real property. The term "real property" means lands, tenements, and all rights pertaining thereto.
Reasonable time or notice. The term "reasonable time or notice" means only such time as may be necessary for the prompt performance of the act required.
Resolution. The term "resolution" means a legislative act of the governing body of a special or temporary character.
Shall or will. These terms mean that a condition exists or an act or action will take place; these terms are mandatory and unconditional.
Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" means any portion of a street between the curbline and the adjacent property line, intended for the use of the pedestrians, but shall not include any unimproved areas between the curbline and improved walkways.
Signature or subscription. The term "signature" or "subscription" means a mark intended as such when the person cannot write.
State. The term "state" or "this state" means the state of Georgia.
Street. The term "street" means any public way, road, highway, street, avenue, boulevard, parkway, alley, viaduct or bridge, and the approach thereto, within the county.
Tenant or occupant. The term "tenant" or "occupant" means, with regard to a building or land, any person holding a written or oral lease thereof, or who occupies the whole or a part of such building or land, either alone or with others.
Tense. The use of any verb in the present or past tense includes the future when applicable.
Week. The term "week" means seven calendar days.
Written or in writing. The term "written" or "in writing" means printing and any other mode of representing words and letters.
Year. The term "year" means a calendar year.
(Code 2000, §§ 1-102, 1-103)

(a) Regular meetings.
(1) Date and time. Except as otherwise decided by the county board of commissioners (hereinafter sometimes referred to as "board"), the board shall hold regular meetings on the first Tuesday of each month beginning at 10:00 a.m.; provided, however, that when the day fixed for any regular meeting of the board falls upon a day designated by law as a legal or national holiday, or for any good reason as determined by the board, such meeting shall be held at the same hour on the second Tuesday of said month.
(2) Place. Except as otherwise decided by the board, all regular meetings of the board shall be held in the Morgan County Courthouse, lower courtroom, 149 E. Jefferson St., Madison, Morgan County, Georgia.
(3) Meeting notice. The time, place, and dates of regular meetings shall be posted and maintained in a conspicuous place available to the public at the regular meeting place of the board.
(b) Special meetings. The chairperson of the board shall call special meetings of the board whenever in his or her opinion the public business may require it, or at the express oral or written request of any three members of the board. Whenever a special meeting is called, the clerk of the board or the clerk's assistant shall notify each member of the board and any other entity legally required to be notified. Whenever any meeting required to be open to the public is to be held at the time and place other than at the time and place prescribed for regular meetings, the clerk or the clerk's assistant shall post a written notice for at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting at the place of regular meetings and by giving written or oral notice to the legal organ of the county. When special circumstances occur, a meeting may be held with less than 24 hours' notice upon giving such notice of the meeting and subjects expected to be considered at the meeting as is reasonable under the circumstances including notice to said legal organ or a newspaper having a general circulation in the county at least equal to that of the legal organ.
(c) Agenda. All reports, communications, ordinances, resolutions, contract documents, or other matters to be submitted to the board shall, if practicable prior to each board meeting, be delivered to the clerk, whereupon said clerk shall immediately arrange a list of such matters according to the order of business, post a copy of the same at the meeting site, and furnish each member of the board with a copy of the same prior to the board meeting and as far in advance of the meeting as time for preparation will permit. All persons wishing to speak to the board or be placed on the agenda shall so notify the said clerk at least 46 business hours prior to the board meeting. No matter not on the said agenda shall be considered by the board and no person not on said agenda shall speak to the board unless a majority of the members of the board vote to do otherwise.
(d) Election and duties.
(1) Election of chairperson. The chairperson shall be elected annually at the first meeting in January of each year by the members of the board. Voting for the chairperson shall be conducted the same as any other matter before the board: by motion/nomination, second, and vote, except that all five commissioners shall be entitled to make motions and vote for the chairperson. The county manager shall serve as the moderator for the board during this process of electing the chairperson. The chairperson shall assume his or her chair immediately after his or her election.
(2) Election of vice-chairperson. Immediately after the election of the chairperson, the members of the board shall elect a vice-chairperson, who shall serve as chairperson in the event of the absence of the chairperson. Voting for vice-chairperson shall be conducted in the same manner as for chairperson, except that the newly elected chairperson shall preside over that matter. All commissioners, including the chairperson, shall be entitled to move, second, and to vote for vice-chairperson.
(3) Chairperson's duties. The chairperson shall be the presiding officer of the board and shall preserve strict order and decorum at all regular and special meetings of the board. He or she shall state every question coming before the board, announce the decision of the board on all subjects, and decide all questions of order, subject, however, to an appeal to the board in which event a majority vote of the board shall govern and conclusively determine such question of order. He or she shall not vote on any question, other than the election of chairperson and vice-chairperson, except in the event of a tie vote.
(4) Appointment of other officials. At the conclusion of voting for chairperson and vice-chairperson, the county attorney, county physician and any other county official shall be appointed by the board during its public meeting.
(e) Call to order; presiding officer. The chairperson, or, in his or her absence, the vice-chairperson, shall take the chair at the hour appointed for the meeting, and shall call the board to order. In the absence of the chairperson or vice-chairperson, the county clerk, or the clerk's assistant, shall call the board to order, whereupon a temporary chairperson shall be elected by the members of the board present. Upon the arrival of the chairperson or vice-chairperson, the temporary chairperson shall immediately relinquish the chair upon the conclusion of the business immediately before the board.
(f) Roll call. Before proceeding with the business of the board, the county clerk or the clerk's deputy may call the roll of the members, and the names of those present shall be entered in the minutes.
(g) Quorum. A majority of all the members elected to the board shall constitute a quorum at any regular or special meeting of the board. In the absence of a quorum, the presiding officer shall, at the insistence of any two members present, compel the attendance of absent members.
(h) Order of business. At the hour set by law on the day of each regular meeting, the members of the board shall take their regular stations in the board chambers, and the business of the board shall generally be taken up for consideration and disposition and may use the following as a guide as to order:
(1) Roll call;
(2) Approval of minutes of previous meeting;
(3) Petitions, remonstrances and communications;
(4) Introduction and adoption of resolutions and ordinances;
(5) Report of officers, boards and committees;
(6) Unfinished business;
(7) New business;
(8) Miscellaneous;
(9) Appropriations;
(10) Adjournment.
(i) Reading of minutes. Unless a reading of the minutes of a board meeting is requested by a member of the board, such minutes may be approved without reading.
(j) Rules of debate.
(1) Presiding officer may debate and vote, etc. The chairperson or such other member of the board as may be presiding may move, second and debate from the chair, subject only to such limitations of debate as are by these rules imposed on all members and shall not be deprived of any of the rights and privileges of a board member by reason of his or her action as the presiding officer except as otherwise specified in this section.
(2) Obtaining the floor; improper references to be avoided. Every member desiring to speak shall address the chair, and, upon recognition by the presiding officer, shall confine himself or herself to the question under debate, avoiding all personalities and indecorous language.
(3) Interruptions. A member, once recognized, shall not be interrupted when speaking unless it is to call him or her to order, or as herein otherwise provided. If a member, while speaking, is called to order, he or she shall cease speaking until the question of order is determined, and, if in order, he or she shall be permitted to proceed.
(4) Privilege of closing date. The board member moving the adoption of an ordinance or resolution shall have the privilege of closing the debate.
(5) Motion to reconsider. A motion to reconsider any action taken by the board may be made only on the date such action was taken. It may be made either immediately during the same session, or at a recessed or adjourned session thereof. Such motion must be made by one of the prevailing side, but may be seconded by any member, and may be made at any time and have precedence over all other motions or while a member has the floor; it shall be debatable. Nothing herein shall be construed to prevent any member of the board from making or remaking the same or any other motion at a subsequent meeting of the board.
(6) Remarks of board member when entered in minutes. A board member may request, through the presiding officer, the privilege of having an abstract of his or her statement on any subject under consideration by the board entered in the minutes. If the board consents thereto, such statement shall be entered in the minutes.
(7) Synopsis of debate when entered in minutes. The clerk may be directed by the presiding officer, with consent of the board, to enter in the minutes a synopsis of the discussion on any question coming regularly before the board.
(k) Addressing the board. Any person on the agenda to address the board shall first secure the permission of the presiding officer so to do.
(l) Addressing the board after motion made. After a motion is made by the board, no person shall address the board without first securing the permission of the board so to do.
(m) Manner of addressing board; time limit. Each person addressing the board shall stand, shall give his or her name and address in an audible tone of voice, and, unless further time is granted by the board, shall limit his or her address to ten minutes. All remarks shall be addressed to the board as a body and not to any member thereof. No person, other than the board and the person having the floor, shall be permitted to enter into any discussion, either directly or through a member of the board, without the permission of the presiding officer. No question shall be asked a board member or county official or employee except through the presiding officer.
(n) Silence constitutes affirmative vote. Unless a member of the board states that he or she is not voting, his or her silence shall be recorded as an affirmative vote.
(o) Decorum.
(1) By board members. While the board is in session, the members must preserve order and decorum, and a member shall neither, by conversation or otherwise, delay or interrupt the proceedings or the peace of the board nor disturb any member while speaking or refuse to obey the orders of the board or its presiding officer, except as otherwise herein provided.
(2) By persons. Any person making personal, impertinent or slanderous remarks or who shall become boisterous while addressing the board shall be forthwith, by the presiding officer, barred from further audience before the board, unless permission to continue is granted by a majority vote of the board.
(p) Enforcement of decorum. The sheriff, or such member or members of the sheriff's department as the sheriff may designate, shall be sergeant-at-arms of the board meetings. The sergeant-at-arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the board meeting. Upon instructions of the presiding officer, it shall be the duty of the sergeant-at-arms, or any of them present, to place any person who violates the order and decorum of the meeting under arrest, and cause him or her to be prosecuted under the provisions of this Code, the complaint to be signed by the presiding officer.
(q) Special committees. All special committees shall be appointed by the presiding officer, unless otherwise directed by the board.
(r) Standing committees. The only standing committee of the board shall be the committee of the whole. The chairperson of the board shall be presiding officer of the committee of the whole, and the rules of proceedings in the board shall be observed in the committee of the whole as far as the same may be applicable.
(s) Members may file protests against board action. Any member shall have the right to have the reasons for his or her dissent from, or protest against, any action of the board entered on the minutes.
(t) Reports of committees. The committee of the whole shall make its reports in writing, and shall return the petition, ordinance, resolution, account, or other paper submitted for consideration.
(u) Reports and resolutions to be filed with the clerk. All reports, ordinances and resolutions shall be filed with the clerk and entered on the minutes.
(v) Adjournment. A motion to adjourn shall always be in order and decided without debate.
(w) Legal effect. Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, a majority of a quorum at any regular or special meeting of the board may vary any and all provisions of this article. The legal effect of any action taken by the board at any regular or special meeting shall not be affected in any way by the failure of the board to follow any rule or provision of this article unless the board's minutes show such failure was brought to the attention of the board at said meeting prior to the taking of the subject action.
(Code 2000, § 3-205; Ord. of 1-10-2006, § 1(3-205))

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, liquors, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, wine, or fortified wine.
Authorized catered function means a function in the unincorporated portions of the county for which an event permit has been issued by the county.
Bed-and-breakfast means a private residence containing no more than ten rooms which may be set aside for overnight guests whose paid accommodations include some meals.
Charitable organization means a nonprofit organization created for charitable purposes, which has received and maintained approval from the United States Internal Revenue Service as a bona fide section 501(c)(3) organization.
Church means a building primarily used for public religious worship on a regular basis.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Food caterer means any person who prepares food for consumption off the premises.
Host means the person who organizes the catered event and who will be responsible, along with the licensed alcohol beverage caterer, for compliance with the rules set forth in this chapter. In the event that the host is an organization rather than an individual, the organization will designate one individual who will be the host for the purposes of this chapter.
License means the authorization by the board of commissioners to engage in the retail sale of malt beverages and/or wine, either in unbroken packages not for consumption on the licensed premises (also referred to hereinafter as a "package license") or for consumption only on the licensed premises (also referred to hereinafter as a "pouring license").
Licensed alcoholic beverage caterer means any retail dealer who has been licensed by the state to sell alcoholic beverages pursuant to O.C.G.A. ch. 4, title 3, art. 2, O.C.G.A. ch. 5, art. 2, or O.C.G.A. ch. 6, art. 2.
Licensed location means the place where a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer maintains its principal place of business within the county.
Licensee means any person who has been issued a license by the board of commissioners to engage in the retail sale of malt beverages and/or wine in unbroken packages not for consumption on the licensed premises (also referred to hereinafter as a "package licensee") or for consumption only on the licensed premises and not for resale (also referred to hereinafter as a "pouring licensee").
Lounge means a separate room where malt beverages and/or wine are served by the drink which is either connected with or part of a restaurant (as defined herein) and operated in conjunction therewith and under the same management as the restaurant operations. Lounges shall not be permitted.
Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Meal means the delivery and service of food in individual portions or by means of a self-service buffet to individual patrons of a place of business. The service of food to a patron shall not constitute a meal if payment for same is combined with payment of a cover charge or entrance fee or if payment for same is in fact merely ancillary to the service of malt beverages and wine. All meals must be prepared in the place of business for which the license is issued.
Minor means any person under the age of 21 years, or as defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-23 or by other state laws.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other entity, group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Place of business means the premises described in the license issued pursuant to this chapter. For the purposes of this chapter, a "place of business" shall consist of one physical building and shall not include any adjacent structures that are not physically attached to the premises by heated and cooled space. Two or more separate, detached structures may not be combined to meet the requirements of this chapter. Outdoor patios or decks which are completely enclosed by a fence or wall and are accessible only through an enclosed building shall be considered as a part of a place of business.
Premises means the location where the licensee is authorized to sell malt beverages and/or wine.
Private club means a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the state, actively in operation within the county at least one year immediately prior to the application for a license hereunder, having at least 100 members regularly paying monthly, quarterly or semiannual dues, organized and operated exclusively for pleasure, recreation and other nonprofit purposes, no part of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any shareholder or member, and owning, hiring or leasing a building or space therein for the reasonable use of its members with suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment and maintaining and using a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing and serving meals at least five days a week for its members and guests. Such club shall also be an organization which has received and has maintained approval from the United States Internal Revenue Service as a bona fide section 501(c)(3) organization. The building of such club shall be air-conditioned. To qualify as a private club under this chapter, no member or officer, agent or employee of the club may be paid, or directly or indirectly receive, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages by the club to its members or guests beyond the amount of such salary as may be fixed by its members at any annual meeting or by its governing board out of the general revenue of the club. No license shall be issued to any location or maintained at any location that does not have adequate on-premises parking as required by the then applicable parking regulations of the board of commissioners.
Restaurant means any public or private place kept, used, maintained, advertised and held out to the general public as a place where meals are served and where meals are actually and regularly served, without sleeping accommodations. Such place shall be air-conditioned and contain adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining room equipment and seating capacity for at least 40 people, and have employed therein a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook and serve suitable food for its patrons. At least two distinct and separate meals per day shall be served at least five days a week, with the exception of holidays, vacations and periods of redecorating or renovation. The serving of such meals and food shall be the principal business conducted, with the serving of malt beverages and/or wine to be consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto. A restaurant shall derive at least 60 percent of its total annual gross food and nonalcoholic beverages sales from the sale of prepared meals or prepared food and shall have food sales in excess of $100,000.00 per year. The term "gross food and nonalcoholic beverage sales" shall not include or be combined with any receipts for cover charges or entrance fees.
Retailer or retail dealer means, except as to distilled spirits, any person who sells alcoholic beverages, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only to consumers and not for resale. With respect to distilled spirits, the term means any person who sells distilled spirits in unbroken packages at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
School means a building, publicly or privately owned, which is used for teaching or giving instruction in any subject to pupils of the school. The term "school" shall not mean a private residential dwelling in which a child receives home schooling from a parent or other person.
Wholesaler means any person who sells malt beverages and/or wine to other wholesale or retail dealers, or licensees.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this chapter.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(2), 32-205(2), 32-205A(1); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(2), 32-205(2), 32-205A(1); Ord. No. 2012-004, § 1, 11-6-2012)

No applicant who has a conviction of or has pled nolo contendre within the previous ten years of the date of application to a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude shall be granted a license if such conviction tends to indicate that the applicant would not maintain the operation for which a license is being sought in conformity with the laws and regulations of the federal or state governments, or the laws and regulations of the county. No license shall be granted to an applicant who has been convicted under any federal, state or local law for a criminal offense involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or tax law violations if such conviction tends to indicate that the applicant would not maintain the operation for which a license is being sought in conformity with the laws and regulations of the federal or state governments, or the laws and regulations of the county.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(F), 32-205(30); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(F), 32-205(30))
153:
Any applicant denied a license shall be prohibited from applying for another license for a period of one year from the filing date set forth on the application. Any partnership, company, corporation, trust or other entity in which an individual applicant is a member, shareholder, director or officer, or in which such entity acts as a surrogate for such applicant, shall also be subject to the prohibition contained in this section.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(O), 32-205(6)(K); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(O), 32-205(6)(K))
154:
(a) If the applicant is a partnership or limited liability company, all members of the partnership must be qualified to obtain a license and must make sworn statements of these qualifications.
(b) If the applicant is a corporation, the manager of the proposed licensed premises must be qualified to obtain a license and must make a sworn statement of these qualifications. A corporate license applicant shall appoint and designate to the board of commissioners an agent authorized to receive service of process under the laws of the state. If no such designation is made, the board may serve or notify the applicant or license holder at any address of the applicant or license holder known to the board.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(I), (J), 32-205(6)(N), (O); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(I), (J), 32-205(6)(N))
155:
A license may be denied to any applicant where it appears that the applicant would not have adequate financial participation in the proposed business to direct and manage its affairs, or where it appears that the applicant is intended to be a mere surrogate for a person who would not otherwise qualify for a license for any reason whatsoever.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(K), 32-205(6)(F); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(K), 32-205(6)(F))
158:
Application for a license shall be made on forms furnished by the board of commissioners according to the following guidelines:
(1) All license applications shall be presented in person to the clerk.
(2) In addition to the completion and submission of an application form as required by the board, each applicant shall attach thereto a completed form with all attachments and requirements for a state license.
(3) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2, the applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints to be forwarded to the state bureau of investigation, which shall search the files of the state crime information center for any instance of criminal activity during the two years immediately preceding the date of the application. The state bureau of investigation shall also submit the fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation under the rules established by the United States Department of Justice for processing and identification of records. The federal record, if any, shall be obtained and returned to the board.
(4) All licenses shall be valid only for the calendar year indicated thereon and no such license may be renewed. A licensee who desires to continue in business during the next calendar year must make a new application for such year to the clerk prior to November 15 of the present year.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(5); 32-205(4); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(5), 32-205(4))
161:
(a) A separate license shall be required for each place of business, as defined herein.
(b) In addition, each pouring license granted will enable the licensee to sell the malt beverages and wine for consumption only in the areas of the premises allowed by state statutory laws and regulations.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(D), 32-205(8); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(D), 32-205(8))
162:
(a) No license shall be issued to any person making a first-time application for a particular location unless complete and detailed diagrams of the building in which the business will be located and the outside premises are attached to the application, or unless proposed plans and specifications and a building permit of a proposed building to be built are attached to the application. If a person is making application for a renewal license for a location for which a license was granted for the previous year, such person shall sign an affidavit, under oath, in lieu of submitting the aforesaid plans and specifications, that there has been no change in the plans of said building. The completed building or the proposed building shall comply with all ordinances of the board of commissioners, rules and regulations of the state revenue commissioner, and the statutory laws of the state. Upon completion, the proposed building shall be subject to final inspection and approval by the building inspector.
(b) Each applicant for a license shall attach to his or her application evidence of ownership of the building or proposed building, or a copy of the lease if the applicant is leasing the building.
(c) Licensees shall provide on the premises for which the license is issued adequate sanitary toilet facilities as required by the health and building codes, and the building shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways and open areas may be clearly seen by customers therein.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(E), 32-205(9); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(E), 32-205(9))
163:
No license shall be granted to any person unless the entire business premises of the proposed location is situated beyond 100 yards from the property line of any church and not less than 200 yards from any schoolyard or college campus, and not less than 100 yards from any building used as an alcohol rehabilitation center. The distance shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground. Each first-time application for a package or pouring malt beverage and wine license shall include a scale drawing of the location of the proposed premises showing the distance to the nearest church, school, and alcohol rehabilitation center and a certificate of a registered surveyor that such location complies with this section.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(C), 32-205(10); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(C), 32-205(10))
164:
The business premises of the licensee shall be made available for inspection at any and all times by officers or officials authorized to conduct such inspections.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(15), 32-205(20); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(15), 32-205(20))
165:
No licensee shall furnish, sell or offer for sale any malt beverages and/or wine under this chapter at any of the following times:
(1) At any time on Christmas Day; or
(2) At any time in violation of a state statutory law, state rules or regulations, local ordinance or regulations.
Licensees holding a license for sale of malt beverages and wine for consumption off premises ("package sales") may sell such beverages on Sundays in compliance with all other applicable state laws. However, sales for consumption on premises ("pouring sales") and sales by alcoholic beverage caterers are prohibited on Sundays.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(b)(ii—iv), 32-205(11); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(b)(ii—iv), 32-205(11); Ord. No. 2012-003, § 1(exh. A), 10-2-2012)
166:
There shall be no gambling, betting, games of chance, punch boards, vending machines, slot machines, pinball machines, lotteries, or tickets of chance therein or the operation of any schemes for hazarding money or any other thing of value in any licensee's place of business or any room adjoining the same, owned, leased, or controlled by the licensee; provided, however, that the sale of state lottery tickets in compliance with O.C.G.A. § 50-27-1 et seq., shall be permitted.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(16), 32-205(23); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(16), 32-205(23))
169:
(a) The board of commissioners, in its discretion, may consider any and all relevant and extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, application or the proposed location of the business. If, in the judgment of the board of commissioners, circumstances are such that the granting, suspension or revocation of the license would or would not be in the best interest of the general public, then such circumstances may be grounds for the denial of the application.
(b) Any misstatement, false statement, or concealment of fact in the application shall be grounds for the denial of the application for license issuance or revocation of the license issued and shall make the applicant liable to prosecution for perjury under the laws of the state.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(L), (M), 32-205(6)(G), (22); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(L), (M), 32-205(6)(G), (22))
170:
The board of commissioners shall give notice in writing to the applicant of any decision to grant or deny an application. The notice shall give the reason for the decision. Notice shall be given by personal service or by certified mail, return receipt requested.
(Code 2000, § 32-205(6)(I); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-205(6)(I))
171:
(a) Whenever the board of commissioners shall deny an application for a package license or pouring license, the applicant shall have ten days following the date of receipt of such notice of the denial to request a hearing before the board. If a hearing is requested, the following information shall be given to the applicant, in writing, by personal service or by certified mail, return receipt requested, at least ten days prior to the hearing date:
(1) The date, time and location of the hearing, said hearing date not to be more than 20 days from the date of said written notice;
(2) A written statement of the reason for the proposed denial of the application;
(3) A list of witnesses, if any, the board of commissioners expects to testify or offer evidence in favor of the denial of the application; and
(4) Notice of the applicant's right to attend the hearing, to present evidence and testimony, to assert any defense of the application, to confront and cross examine anyone who would testify in favor of denial of application and to have an attorney present to represent the applicant.
(b) Any decision denying an application shall set forth the reason for such action in writing, which shall be delivered by regular mail to the applicant's address set forth in the application.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(N), 32-205(6)(J); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(N), 32-205(6)(J); Ord. of 4-1-2008(2), §§ 1, 2)
174:
(a) Except as otherwise stated in this section, no package or pouring license shall be transferable or assignable to any person or other location, and in the event that a licensed business is sold or closed, it shall be the duty of the licensee to immediately surrender said license to the board of commissioners. Under no circumstances will the license fee be refunded to the holder.
(b) All holders of licenses issued under this section shall, within six months after the issuance of such license, open for business the establishment referred to in the license. Failure to open the licensed establishment within such period shall serve as a forfeiture and cancellation of the unused license and no refund of the license fee shall be made to the license holder.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(13), 32-205(7); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(13), 32-205(7))
177:
The licensee shall be responsible for the management and operation of the business for which the license is granted and shall be responsible for all violations of this chapter by the licensee's agents and employees.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(4)(G), 32-205(6)(L); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(4)(G), 32-205(6)(L))
178:
No licensee shall buy or arrange to buy or in any way cause the transfer of any malt beverages and/or wine except from a licensed wholesaler. A licensee under this chapter shall take delivery only at the licensed place of business from a licensed wholesaler or licensed common carrier acting for a licensed wholesaler. A licensee shall comply with all other requirements, including, without limitation, those set forth at Chapters 560-2 (Ga. Comp Rules and Regs. 560-2-1 et seq., Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division) and 560-8 (Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. 560-8-1 et seq., Alcohol and Tobacco Tax Division—Malt Beverages, Wine, Tobacco) of the Georgia Administrative Code, as well as the rules and regulations of the state department of revenue.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(D), 32-204(31), 32-205(44), 32-205(46); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(D), 32-204(31), 32-205(44), 32-205(46))
179:
A licensee shall keep no inventory or stock of malt beverages and/or wine at any place except the licensed place of business, and within the licensed place of business the storage area for malt beverages and/or wine shall be immediately adjacent to and attached to the retail area or area of consumption. No licensee shall enter into any type of arrangement whereby malt beverages and/or wine ordered by the licensee are stored by a licensed wholesaler.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(E), (33), 32-205(45); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(E), (33), 32-205(45))
180:
A license issued under this chapter shall be displayed prominently at all times on the premises for which it was issued.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(8), 32-205(25); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(8), 32-205(25))
181:
(a) All premises used for the sale and/or consumption of malt beverages and/or wine, and/or for the storage of malt beverages and/or wine, shall be kept in a sanitary condition and shall be kept in full compliance with the regulations of the county health department.
(b) All licensed premises shall be subject to inspection by the health department, all county fire departments, the building inspector, and all authorized law or code enforcement officers to determine if the premises are in compliance with all county, state and federal rules, regulations, laws and codes.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(23), 32-205(33); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(23), 32-205(33))
182:
A licensee shall maintain on the premises at all times a telephone in good working order.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(F), 32-205(34); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(F), 32-205(34))
183:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee to knowingly allow any person with a criminal record for violence or disorder to frequent the licensed premises or loiter on the premises.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(G), 32-205(27); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(G), 32-205(27))
184:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee to knowingly allow any person to frequent the licensed premises for the purpose of soliciting prostitution.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(H), 32-205(28); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(H), 32-205(28))
185:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee to fail to report to the police at the earliest possible time any known incident of a criminal nature that occur on the licensed premises. It shall be unlawful for any licensee to willfully withhold from the police any information pertaining to any crime that may have occurred on the licensed premises.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(7)(I), 32-205(29); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(7)(I), 32-205(29))
186:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee to knowingly allow any criminal act to be committed on the licensed premises.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(7)(J); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(7)(J))
187:
In addition to the rules and regulations set out in this chapter, each licensee under this chapter shall comply with all statutory laws of the state, all federal statutory laws, and all rules and regulations of the state revenue commissioner relating to the sale and distribution of malt beverages and/or wine in the state; and any violation of same shall subject said licensee to suspension or revocation of his or her license and also may subject said licensee to criminal prosecution by the proper authority as provided by law and the ordinances of the county.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(17); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(17))
188:
In conjunction with any license application or any license issued under the terms hereof, or in conjunction with the revocation, suspension or cancellation of any license or in conjunction with any of the hearings contemplated by this chapter, or in conjunction with the payment or nonpayment of any excise tax levied or to be collected hereunder, the board of commissioners shall have the right to subpoena all or any part of the records, books, documents, reports or invoices of any applicant or licensee. Said subpoena right shall be had for the purposes of auditing the records of such applicant or licensee, securing compliance by such licensee with the provisions of this chapter, proving or disproving violation of any part of this chapter by any licensee, or to show payment or nonpayment of any taxes, fees, charges or the like due hereunder.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(22), 32-205(21); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(22), 32-205(21))
189:
All licensees shall keep a copy of this chapter on the licensed premises and shall instruct any person working there about compliance with the terms hereof. Each licensee and the licensee's agents selling packaged malt beverages and/or wine, or selling for consumption on the premises malt beverages and/or wine, shall at all times be familiar with the terms hereof. The licensee shall be held responsible for any acts of the licensee's agents and employees which are in violation of this chapter, the statutory laws of the state, and/or the rules and regulations of the state revenue commissioner.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(26), 32-205(19); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(26), 32-205(19))
190:
The licensee shall post in a conspicuous place in his or her establishment a sign printed in letters at least four inches high reading as follows: "SALE OF BEER AND WINE TO PERSONS UNDER 21 YEARS OF AGE STRICTLY PROHIBITED." The licensee shall also post in a conspicuous place in the licensed premises a sign printed in letters at least four inches high reading as follows: "WARNING: DRINKING BEER AND WINE DURING PREGNANCY CAN CAUSE BIRTH DEFECTS."
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(27), 32-205(13); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(27), 32-205(13); Ord. No. 2012-003, § 1(exh. A), 10-2-2012)
191:
No licensee nor any agent or employee of a licensee shall furnish, sell or offer to sell any malt beverage and/or wine to any person who is confined in any jail, penal institution, correctional facility, prison camp, penitentiary or other lawful place of confinement, or to any person who is a patient or inmate of the Central State Hospital, or to any person who is noticeably intoxicated, or is of unsound mind, or is a habitual drunkard whose intemperate habits are known to the licensee or the agent or employee.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(28), 32-205(14); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(28), 32-205(14))
192:
All malt beverages and/or wine shall be under lock or fully covered by opaque material during those hours when their sale is not permitted except in the event of an emergency or under the direction of a law enforcement official, county official or his or her designate. All malt beverages and/or wine owned or possessed contrary to the provisions of this chapter are hereby declared to be contraband and shall be seized by the proper authorities.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(29), 32-205(40); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(29), 32-205(40))
193:
It shall be unlawful for licensees or their agents or employees to add to the contents of a container or to refill empty containers or in any manner to misrepresent the quantity, quality or brand name of any malt beverage and/or wine.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(30), 32-205(32); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(30), 32-205(32))
196:
(a) Every licensee under this chapter shall maintain at all times on the premises for which the license has been issued a list of all persons currently employed by such licensee at such premises, which list shall show the current full legal name, alias, date of birth, current address, current home telephone number and social security number of each employee.
(b) The employee list shall be available during reasonable hours for inspection by any law enforcement officer or county official or his or her designee. If so required by such person, an employee must submit to a fingerprint identification and criminal history check. Every licensee shall cause each of the licensee's employees during the hours of his or her employment to be identified by a conspicuous label or badge upon which shall appear the employee's first name.
(c) No person under 21 years of age shall be employed in any capacity in any place of business licensed under this section. No holder of a pouring license shall employ, require or permit a person under 21 years of age to sell or take orders for malt beverages and/or wine. However, persons under 21 years of age who are employed in supermarkets, convenience stores, breweries and drugstores that are licensed to engage in the retail sale of malt beverages and/or wine in unbroken packages and not for consumption on the premises may sell or handle malt beverages and/or wine which are sold pursuant to and in compliance with this chapter.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any licensee to employ on the premises any person who, in the preceding ten years, has been convicted of a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude in the state or who has been convicted of a crime outside the state which would be a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude in the state.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(25), 32-205(36); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(25), 32-205(36))
199:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a minor to attempt to purchase malt beverages and/or wine or for any other person to purchase malt beverages and/or wine for a minor.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a minor to exhibit fake, forged, or borrowed credentials in an effort to obtain malt beverages and/or wine to which the minor is not legally entitled.
(c) No person engaged in the business regulated hereunder shall make or permit to be made any sale of malt beverages and/or wine to minors.
(d) No person shall allow anyone under 21 years of age to loiter about the premises of the licensee or possess any alcoholic beverage. This provision shall not apply to employees over the age of 18 years eligible for subject employment under the laws of the state.
(e) Any violations of the provisions of this division shall constitute a misdemeanor and the offender, upon being found guilty, shall be punishable as for a misdemeanor, and by possible loss of license and fine.
(f) The prohibition contained in this subsection shall not apply with respect to the sale, purchase or possession of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption:
(1) For medical purposes pursuant to a prescription of a physician duly authorized to practice medicine in the state;
(2) At a religious ceremony; or
(3) In the minor's home with parental consent.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(18), 32-205(31); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(18), 32-205(31))
202:
(a) Any violation of one or more provisions of this chapter shall be punishable pursuant to section 1-9, and shall be tried in the magistrate court as set forth in section 1-10.
(b) In addition to any punishment for violating this chapter, any such violation may subject a licensee to the revocation or suspension of his or her license, as set forth in sections 6-301 and 6-302.
(1) Any revocation or suspension based upon a violation of this chapter will subject the licensee to a reinstatement fee between $500.00 and $1,000.00, to be determined in the discretion of the board.
a. This reinstatement fee is non-refundable and must be paid prior to the reinstatement of any license issued under this chapter.
b. No new license shall be issued to a licensee whose previous license was revoked or suspended until the reinstatement fee is paid.
c. Payment of the non-refundable reinstatement fee does not guarantee the reinstatement or issuance of a license, but is instead a condition precedent to the consideration of reinstatement or issuance by the board.
(2) In addition to any other punishments or civil penalties set forth herein, any revocation or suspension based upon a violation of this chapter, may subject a licensee to the forfeiture of all stock of malt beverages and wine.
(3) The following suspension and revocation guidelines apply to a licensee who violates this chapter by selling or allowing the sale at his or her establishment of beer and/or wine to an ineligible individual under this chapter (including but not limited to a minor), sells during hours and/or days on which sales of beer and/or wine are prohibited under this chapter, and/or sells without a valid license, whether suspended, revoked, or not yet issued:
a. For a first offense within the previous five years, a 30-day suspension of his or her license and a reinstatement fee of $500.00.
b. For a second or subsequent offense within five years of a first offense, the revocation of his or her license for the remainder of the year, a reinstatement fee of $1,000.00, and forfeiture of all stock in malt beverages and wine.
c. These guidelines in subsections i. and ii. above are those a licensee can expect to receive as a minimum, although the board will make the final decision in each instance and has the right to impose differing suspensions, revocations, and reinstatement fees.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(19), 32-205(47); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(19), 32-205(47); Ord. of 4-1-2008(2), §§ 1, 2)
204:
(a) Whenever the board of commissioners wishes to take any action to suspend or revoke any license issued hereunder, the board shall provide ten days' written notice, by personal service or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the licensee prior to taking such action. The notice shall set forth the reasons for such action. The licensee shall have ten days from the date of receipt of such notification of such action (as set forth on the aforesaid receipt) to request a hearing before the board. Said notification shall be in writing and shall be delivered to the board by hand delivery or by certified mail, return receipt requested.
(b) If a hearing is requested, the following information shall be given to the licensee, in writing, by regular mail to the licensee's last known address, at least ten days prior to the hearing date:
(1) A written copy of all charges or reasons for the proposed suspension or revocation;
(2) The date, time and location of the hearing, said hearing date to be not more than 20 days from the date of said written notice;
(3) A list of witnesses, if any, the board expects to testify or offer evidence in favor of the suspension or revocation; and
(4) Notice of the licensee's right to attend the hearing, to present evidence and testimony, to assert any defense, to confront and cross examine opposing witnesses, and to have an attorney present to represent the licensee.
(c) All decisions suspending or revoking a license shall set forth the reason for such action in writing, and shall be delivered to the licensee at his or her last known address by regular mail.
(Code 2000, §§ 32-204(21), 32-205(43); Ord. of 11-2-2004, §§ 32-204(21), 32-205(43); Ord. of 4-1-2008(2), §§ 1, 2)
206:
Footnote 2:
State Law reference— Governing authority of county has power to locally regulate, license, and tax the manufacturing, distribution and selling of malt beverages, O.C.G.A. §§ 3-5-40 et seq., 3-5-80 et seq.; governing authority of county has power to locally regulate, license, and tax the manufacturing, distribution and selling of wine, O.C.G.A. §§ 3-6-40 et seq., 3-6-60 et seq.
207:
Malt beverages and/or wine sold pursuant to a package license granted under this chapter will be for consumption only off the premises of the licensee.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(3); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(3))
208:
Before any package license is granted, the applicant must post with the board of commissioners, along with the application, a cash bond or performance bond with an insurance company as surety. Said bond shall require the faithful observance and performance by the licensee of the rules and regulations contained in this section. Upon the violation of this section, or any part thereof, the amount of the bond to be forfeited will be determined by the seriousness of the violation as determined by the board. Said bond is to be approved by the board and shall be properly executed. Said bond shall be in the amount of $2,500.00 for a wholesale permit and $500.00 for a retail license.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(5)(d); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(5)(d))
209:
The annual fee for a license shall be $500.00 per annum and shall be paid after acceptance and approval of the application by the board of commissioners, but prior to the issuance of such license. The fee shall be paid either in cash or by bank certified check. All licenses shall expire on December 31 of the year for which they were granted. No license fee shall be prorated.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(6); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(6))
210:
(a) No licensee shall sell or deliver any malt beverages and/or wine to any person except in the licensee's place of business. A licensee shall be permitted to load purchased goods in a customer's vehicle when the sale physically takes place and monies have been exchanged inside the place of business. A licensee may have a drive-in window and may deliver packaged malt beverages and/or wine through such window. Said drive-in window must be visible from the nearest street. "Curb service" type sales and sales to customers in vehicles parked in the parking area of the place of business are prohibited.
(b) No licensee shall furnish, sell or offer for sale any malt beverages and/or wine at any times except:
(1) Between 6:00 a.m. and 11:45 p.m. on Mondays through Saturday; and
(2) Between 12:30 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. on Sundays.
(c) No person shall sell or possess for the purpose of sale, any malt beverages and/or wine where such person does not have a license from the board of commissioners to sell or possess for sale such beverages and/or wine.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(7), (32); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(7), (32); Ord. No. 2012-003, § 1(exh. A), 10-2-2012)
211:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-4-49, no license shall be granted to any person authorizing the location of a new retail package liquor licensed place of business or the relocation of an existing retail package liquor licensed place of business engaged in the retail package sales of distilled spirits within 500 yards of any other business licensed to sell package liquor at retail, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(4)(C); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(4)(C))
212:
Any wholesale distributor in malt beverages and wine licensed by the state or the agent of such licensed wholesale distributor may be granted a permit to distribute such malt beverages and wine in the county, upon application for such permit to the clerk, and upon the presentation of evidence satisfactory to said county that the applicant understands and will comply with all terms and conditions and provisions of the chapter governing the package sale of malt beverages and wine in the county, as said chapter may be amended, including, but not limited to, those under which malt beverages and wine licenses are issued, and upon payment of an annual fee of $100.00 for malt beverage wholesale distributors pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-5-43, a fee of $500.00 for wine wholesale distributors and a fee of $600.00 for wholesale distributors of both beer and wine; provided, however, that malt beverage wholesale distributors who have their principal place of business in the county shall pay an annual fee of $2,500.00.
(Code 2000, § 32-204(9); Ord. of 11-2-2004, § 32-204(9))
213:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-5-80 and O.C.G.A. § 3-5-81, there is hereby levied upon wholesale malt beverages distributors a tax on malt beverages as follows:
